racecards.race_name: Balnakeilly Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Has a very solid record here and could play a leading role if fully tuned up after a break
runners.spotlight: Made a good start to his chasing career last year, winning three times between May and September (2m3f/2m4f, good), with two of them over C&D; also effective on good to soft, unproven on softer; he has a very solid record here and could play a leading role if fully tuned up after a break.

quotes.race: Francky Du Berlais Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I couldn't believe King Roly was backed so much. The way he was jumping over fences at home was electric. He was a bit sticky early on, but he warmed to it. I think he'll be a good chaser, he stays all day and will be the type for a summer national - Mickey Bowen, trainer,

stable_tour.quote: There's a novice handicap chase at Perth at their three-day festival next month that he'll go for. He's really well and I'm hoping he'll keep on improving throughout the late spring and summer months. I'm sure he could be one of ours to go for the Summer Plate at Market Rasen. 26-03-26

runners.comment: Soundly beaten on last two starts but in tougher races; he remains one to be interested in
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten on last two starts but those were Class 2 contests at Cheltenham and Kempton and this is a drop back in grade; this lightly raced 7yo had previously made a promising start to his chasing career, including a 2m4f win at Kempton, and he remains one to be interested in.

quotes.race: "Get Your Ladbrokes Free Kempton Bet" Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Barlovento went round well and Sean [Bowen] said he's a horse who would handle better ground and two and a half miles round here well. He's a horse I got completely wrong as I thought he'd wanted deep ground and a trip. I thought he was an absolute certainty in a novice hurdle at Warwick last season, and I was very disappointing leaving the track that day. He'd want to go up 8lb or 9lb, but he'd need to run again to qualify for the Jack Richards [Novice Handicap Chase] at Cheltenham. He's a horse who will keep improving - Olly Murphy, trainer.Barlovento is a brilliant jumper and the first thing I said to Olly [Murphy] after riding him at Exeter was 'Sorry, that was the worst ride I've ever given a horse!' Thankfully he has repaid us today. The ground is quick and I thought we went steady there to be honest. We quickened sharply turning in. The fences have actually made this horse quicker. He's a proper two and a half miler - he travelled well and did it well - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Get The Inside Track With raceday-ready.com Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 3 Elim') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Barlovento was in front for a long time and got lonely but we've always liked him and he's got a bright future. He's for sale and will hopefully be in different colours next time he's on a racecourse - Olly Murphy, trainer.

runners.comment: Just one run this season, when soundly beaten on chase debut, but he's not written off
runners.spotlight: Point (3m, soft to heavy) and two-time novice hurdle (2m3f/2m4f, good/good to soft) winner; he's run just once this season, when 14l fourth of six on chase debut at Aintree (2m4f, soft) in December; however, he remains very lightly raced and is certainly not written off today.

stable_tour.quote: The race he won at Lingfield last week cut up but he had to do the donkey work and quickened up well in the straight. We're not getting carried away, but he'll improve dramatically for his first run and looks like he has a bright future. 21-11-24

runners.breeder: Philippe Thiriet & S C E A Haras De Pey

prev_owners.owner: Scea Haras De Peyre, Y Fouin & Mme Pascale Papon

runners.comment: Runner-up at Ayr in January but three lesser efforts have followed; has to raise his game
runners.spotlight: Runner-up when back over fences at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in January and this 6yo is of interest on that form; however, three lesser performances have followed and he needs to raise his game if he's to win this.

quotes.race: ClonmelRaces.ie (Q.R.) Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Karafon jumped brilliant, settled great and his form entitled him to do it like that. He'll step up in grade now - Patrick Mullins, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He's still a novice over hurdles and quite a nice one. I think a fair bit of him, so I wouldn't be afraid to aim him at some of the decent novice hurdles. 25-11-24

runners.comment: Improvement needed on third chase start but yard's horses always worth a second look here
runners.spotlight: 9yo who is lightly raced for his age; he needs to produce more than he managed at Leopardstown and Downpatrick last month on his first two chase starts but he wears first-time headgear today and Gordon Elliott's horses are always well worth a second look at Perth; could have a big say.

quotes.race: Easter Festival April 19th - 21st Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Find A Fortune looked big enough for one of ours and I thought he might need the run. He handles better ground so we will keep him going over hurdles - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's better than he showed in a Clonmel bumper. He's a nice horse and should be able to win a maiden hurdle this winter. 24-10-23

He's a great big Walk In The Park who we like a lot. He won well at Ayr, but he wasn't right when he went to Haydock and we never really got him back afterwards. He's every inch a chaser and could leave his hurdles form behind. 29-10-25

runners.breeder: P Noue & S A R L Ecurie Silgezam
runners.comment: Runner-up at Ayr in January but pulled up at Carlisle since and needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 8yo who was runner-up at Ayr (2m, soft) in January when dropped back in trip on his second chase start; however, pulled up at Carlisle (2m, good to soft) since, which severely dents confidence in his claims today, and the step up in distance may not be ideal.

stable_tour.quote: I love him, he's a little dude. He's not the biggest but he's really well put together. He's owned by Darren Mills Racing and he owned Rapid Flight, who we've just had to retire due to an injury he picked up in last season's Becher Chase. It's nice he's got another good horse. This one ran a little bit green when winning at Hexham and then won well enough at Kelso. He's a brilliant jumper, he's tough and he stays three miles all day long. He's peaking now and I'm really pleased with him. He's from the same family as Princess Zoe, so it's a lovely pedigree. He'll go to Haydock on Saturday for the Albert Bartlett trial, a race we won with Chief Dan George, and we'll dip our toe in the water to see where we are. He's got the entry in the main race at Cheltenham and will go there if he comes through his test at Haydock. There's a possibility we might look at the Sefton at Aintree, but it's one step at a time. He'll go chasing next season when his jumping will stand him in good stead. 14-02-24

prev_owners.owner: G R Orchard And Annie Mania

runners.comment: 3-5 since cheekpieces went on, the latest win on Monday; 7lb penalty might not stop him
runners.spotlight: Three wins (2m3f-2m7f, soft-good) from his five starts since these cheekpieces went on, the latest in gutsy fashion at Kelso on Monday when clear with a rejuvenated runner-up; a 7lb penalty might not stop this progressive 7yo if today's assignment doesn't come too soon.

quotes.race: Racing Post+ Subscription Go North Monet's Garden Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Wolfburg's been a different horse since he's gone chasing. This is easily the best day of the season. It's all just come together. It's been a brilliant weekend, winning a bumper as well with King Kubala, who's going to be a proper horse. We've had a rough season, for lots of reasons. The horses haven't been quite right but things are going well now. - Sandy Thomson, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Wolfburg showed a bit of form as a young horse then fell away. They've had some things done to him, his wind and stuff like that, and cheekpieces and fences seemed to help him. On the whole his jumping was very good - Craig Nicol, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He came back from his last run at Carlisle with a bit of an injury, so he's had some time off. He'll be back in work shortly and we'll keep him hurdling now. He needs a bit of time between his races. He was good in a bumper and very good the day he won over hurdles at Catterick last season and you can probably give him excuses for some of his other runs, which have been disappointing. He'll be a cracking novice chaser next season. 22-01-25

racecards.verdict: Gordon Elliott has a very strong record at Perth and FIND A FORTUNE could take a healthy step forward in first-time headgear.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Barlovento, 4/1 King Roly,  Walking On A Dream, 9/2 Find A Fortune, 5/1 It's Hard To Know, 12/1 Karafon,  Great Pepper

racecards.race_name: British EBF Gold Castle 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Grade 2 winner; pulled up at Cheltenham but one to be interested in back in calmer waters
runners.spotlight: Won Grade 2 novice hurdle at Limerick (2m7f, heavy) in December and 8l second in Grade 1 at Leopardstown (2m6f, heavy) in February; pulled up at 25-1 in the Albert Bartlett at Cheltenham (3m, soft) last month but back in calmer waters today and he's one to be interested in given his previous promise.

quotes.race: Defender Novice Hurdle (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: It was a big step up in trip but it was a lovely, tough performance by Kazansky - Danny Gilligan, jockey.

quotes.race: BAR 1 Casino Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: The horse in front looked like he was gone, but it happened to us in the first. We had luck on our side, but Kazansky is a galloper and stays well - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's come a long way in a short space of time. He's a good, solid stayer who won well at Limerick over Christmas and ran well against Doctor Steinberg in a Grade 1 at the Dublin Racing Festival. He's the sort of horse I could see running a big race in the Albert Bartlett. That race should suit him. 09-02-26

runners.owner: McNeill Family And Chris & Giles Barber
runners.comment: Grade 1 winner; disappointing favourite at Cheltenham but the one to beat if back to best
runners.spotlight: Made it 3-3 over hurdles (2m5f/2m4f, soft/good) in ready fashion in the Grade 1 Challow at Newbury in December; very disappointing favourite in the Turners at the Cheltenham Festival, even allowing for what went wrong at the start, but he's the one to beat today if back to his best; promises to be suited by the step up in trip (dam won 3m French Grade 1).

quotes.race: Turners Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (Registered As The Baring Bingham Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The false start hasn't helped anybody. I don't know why they didn't let them go first time. Some of the starts are becoming ludicrous. They could have gone first time. Instead he's started cold, missed the break a bit and with 22 runners you've nowhere to go. I'd have loved to have been where Act Of Innocence was in the first three or four. The race didn't go to plan. Harry got off and said No Drama This End was beat after jump one in the position he was in, and then he's got murdered everywhere he went. He had no chance. It was a painful watch. I thought we were going to jump out very sharp. The most important thing in a field that big is to get a good start and to be sharp, and we didn't get a good start and from there it was all over. He had nowhere to go and everywhere he tried to go he couldn't. On this sort of ground you can't make up that sort of ground, especially if you're getting mullered everywhere. It was all over passing the stands first time. It just didn't work today. It wasn't a case of not being good enough, it just never happened. I don't know if we'll run him again or wait for next season. We could go to Aintree or leave him for chasing. We've trained him for this one day and that's happened. I suspect if we went to Aintree we'd probably go three miles. The only good thing is everything I've ever run in this has got beat and turned out to be a champion - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Challow Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: No Drama This End is right up there with other Challow winners. He's had three runs over hurdles, and he's won two Grade 2s and a Grade 1, and none of them achieved that. I'm not saying he's Denman, but in ten years I might. If I had one that might be like him, if we're lucky, then he could be. He's got it all, and he's exciting. I told Harry [Cobden] to ride him like the best horse in the race, and that was fantastic. He's very special. We'll go straight to the Festival. He's shown he's effective on good ground over two and a half miles, but we'll cover both options. To back him up again, three weeks after another, has not been ideal. It's not been easy to get him right for today, but I can give him a break now and get him better - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Winter Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I read the Racing Post this morning and it said the 0-125 conditional jockeys' race at the November meeting was run four seconds quicker, and I thought 'blimey'. When No Drama This End wins like that you start to question what he's beaten, although I know John McConnell's horse Heads Up is a very good horse, and he can't be a bad horse all of a sudden because we've beaten him. I really wanted to see him do it again. There was a moment on the home turn where I thought, actually this isn't going the way we thought, but it was only about two seconds and he just gathered himself together again. When Harry [Cobden] glanced between his legs down the home straight I thought maybe he is going as well as he looks. I couldn't watch the last two hurdles because I just wanted him to get home, but in the end it was very impressive. I've been lucky enough to have some really good horses but this horse could be special. He's so exciting, I've never had one potentially this good. Whether we have a look at the Challow now is up to Paul [Nicholls] and the team, but I'd be happy either way. All the horses in this race were good horses, but today we just had that bit extra - Max McNeill, co-owner.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Hyde Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We always thought No Drama This End was very nice at home. I was really worried about the ground today for his first run over hurdles, but he did that so well. He's a real class horse and I've waited a long time to have a really classy one since Denman and some of those. I think with a bit of luck he could be one of them. That was a good performance - it was his first run over hurdles, and he can only improve. I'd say we'll head to the Challow with him. He has got the experience now and won't run in between. We need to look after him and what a lovely chaser he will make. It's great for the Barber family to have another really smart horse and Max (McNeill) is involved with him as well. It's brilliant - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Happy New Year From Poundland Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've known about No Drama This End for a long time and we bought him off Will [Biddick] after he won his point-to-point. He did do a very nice racecourse gallop a few weeks ago and we thought he'd run well, but that blew us away. We like him and he'll have a tentative entry for the Cheltenham bumper. If it was soft, we'd possibly consider it. Whether it's there or at Aintree, or somewhere else, he'll have one more run this season then go hurdling in the autumn - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Everyone wants to ask me about him and I've tended to start saying the horse has done all the talking for me. He's had three runs, in Grade 2s twice and a Grade 1, and won them all. The ground was quick enough for him in the Challow, but we let him take his chance and he won nicely. A lot of commentators said it wasn't that impressive, but I thought it was having changed tactics with him and on that ground in a slowly run race. He's got to step up again, but I think he will and soft ground will suit. If the ground is on the slow side of good to soft he'll be in the Turners, and he's not slow. He's got the Albert Bartlett entry just in case. 15-02-26

runners.comment: Impressive in big-field handicap at Fairyhouse this month; respected despite tougher task
runners.spotlight: 5yo who has raced four times, all over hurdles, and he was winning for a second time when powering clear in a big-field handicap at Fairyhouse (3m, yielding to soft) this month; today is a tougher test of his credentials but he was impressive last time and could be up to the task.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Novice Handicap Hurdle Series Final (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I'd say the ground is hard work and Danny took his time. Sept Etoiles was so disappointing the last day, we might look at Punchestown or Ayr for him next, he's a chaser in the making - Gordon Elliott, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Convincing win at Southwell in February and could have lots more to offer for top trainer
runners.spotlight: Left December's debut run (2m5f, good to soft) well behind to win in good style at Southwell (2m4f, soft) in February; faces a much higher calibre of opponent today but he could have lots more to offer for his top trainer.

runners.comment: 2-2 over hurdles; others have stronger form but remains to be seen where limitations lie
runners.spotlight: Point winner who is 2-2 over hurdles following novice wins at Warwick (2m5f, soft) and Wincanton (2m5f, good); others have more substance to their form but he did it easily last time and it remains to be seen where his limitations lie.

quotes.race: Bath & West Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Sogna In Grande got ringworm shortly after he won and it completely knocked him sideways. I don't think I've ever had a horse suffer as bad as him. He's a very nice horse and will be a chaser - Kim Bailey, joint-trainer, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: PricedUp Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This looked a warm contest so to win like that was very pleasing - Tom Bellamy, jockey of Sogna In Grande.

stable_tour.quote: He's a fine, big horse who won a British point-to-point and he's all over a chaser. We thought he'd run well on his rules debut at Warwick in November but were slightly surprised that he won as it looked a very good race on paper. You'll see him over the Christmas period with a penalty, and that will tell us whether he's up to the next level or to go handicapping. He wants a trip and we'll see how we get on. 24-12-25

runners.owner: Cherry Knoll Farm, M Ward & D Skelton

prev_owners.owner: Cherry Knoll Farm, M&T Ward & D Skelton

runners.comment: No match for No Drama This End at Sandown but he's improved since; can go well
runners.spotlight: No match for the winner No Drama This End when 12l fourth of five in Grade 2 at Sandown (2m4f, soft) in December; however, he showed improved form when easily making all in Doncaster novice (3m, good to soft) in February and can give a good account in his rematch; has also won on soft.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tormund Giantsbane is a lovely horse and he'll probably head to Aintree now - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A lovely horse, he took us a little by surprise when he won his bumper at Worcester last autumn, as he looked a big, galloping type. He did well to finish second in his next bumper and scored on his hurdling debut at Carlisle, where he relaxed well, jumped fluently and travelled into the race smoothly. He'll go for the Winter Novices' Hurdle at Sandown on December 5. 10-11-25

racecards.verdict: Preference is for SOGNA IN GRANDE, who did it easily to make it 2-2 over hurdles at Wincanton and could have lots more left in the tank.
racecards.betting_forecast: 8/11 No Drama This End, 7/2 Tormund Giantsbane, 11/2 Sept Etoiles, 10/1 Kazansky, 12/1 Sogna In Grande

racecards.race_name: Fair Maid Of Perth Mares' Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Won this two years ago; just one run this season (November) but can give a good account
runners.spotlight: Consistent sort who won this two years ago (soft); Panic Attack has better form and she's run just once this season, but that was a solid effort when third of five at Carlisle in November over an inadequate 2m4f (good to soft), and she can give a good account.

quotes.race: Robertson Homes Fair Maid Of Perth Mares' Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Apple Away has had a hard season, especially after Cheltenham over three miles and six. She's come out of it really well though and with a bit of sun on her back she looks a picture and proved it out there. I thought it was the best she's jumped since she's gone chasing, Derek gave her a great ride, and it's all come together. She's done everything we could have asked of her this year, so that'll be her finished for the season - Michael Scudamore, assistant trainer

quotes.race: @leicesterraces Christmas Meeting 28th December Book Now Beginners' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was really pleased and it was an ideal race for Apple Away. The ground was probably heavier than she's ever handled, but she was class. We ended up running her at Haydock in a race that was probably too tough for her first time out, so we found this easier for her. It's a great start to her chasing career. She's one of those we could have continued over hurdles with, but I think she can take us to another level over fences. Derek (Fox, jockey) was very impressed. He said she's very clever and she can go short or long. She makes her mind up a long way out, so you just meet the fences correctly with her. He was delighted because he didn't realise quite how far in front he was jumping the last - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Graduation Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: For a first run over fences Apple Away has performed brilliantly. She's been clever in front of a fence, she's got plenty of scope, she needs an extra half mile at least, if not a mile. She's just been outpaced - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Winners Wear Cavani Sefton Novices' Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm so delighted with Apple Away. She's relentless, she just keeps on galloping. Stephen did a very good job of kicking early and getting that lead. I wasn't worried at the last this time, she's a total three-miler. When we came into the race we knew that she had a few pounds to find but the mares' allowance is ideal and she's just got such tenacity and determination which is ideal for this sort of race - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Shade Oak Stud Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Apple Away was very game at the finish. She ran a bit free during the race, but has plenty of ability. She'll do better over fences down the line and stay further as well - Derek Fox, rider.

stable_tour.quote: She's a wonderful mare. She was fortunate to pick up the Grand National Trial and it's obvious to aim towards that again. We probably shouldn't have run her in the Midlands National afterwards as she had a harder race at Haydock than we gave her credit for. You'd love to think she could make up into a Scottish National type as anything at more than three miles suits her very well. 29-10-25

She was successful in a 3m point-to-point in April before coming here and got off to a flyer on her debut under rules for us, winning a novice hurdle by a head at Bangor. She hasn't run a bad race since and her most recent effort when a half-length second to Sacre Coeur at Haydock was very encouraging. She has bags of stamina and for one so inexperienced she jumps beautifully. She could go to Ayr on Valentine's Day, followed by a Listed mares' novice hurdle to try to get her some black type. Next season when she jumps a fence, I think she'll be even better. 25-01-23

runners.comment: Early exit in Grand National 11 days ago; leading claims on the rest of her form this term
runners.spotlight: Ran in the Grand National 11 days ago, badly hampered at the second fence and falling at the third; won two high-profile handicaps last November before Listed win at Newbury and the drop back to 2m4f didn't appear ideal at the Cheltenham Festival; leading claims if none the worse for last time.

quotes.race: Mrs Paddy Power Mares' Chase (Registered As The Liberthine Mares' Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Panic Attack has run a beautiful Grand National trial over two and a half miles. She jumped immaculately. She's a phenomenal jumper and I'm very proud of her. She couldn't quite win today on decent ground but that's sometimes how the cookie crumbles. We'd love to see her jump like that round Aintree wouldn't we. It would be some sight and the dream's alive. It's a possibility. It's not a probability, but it's a possibility - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Alder Demain & Akers Mares' Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: On the numbers, Panic Attack ought to have done that, but it was fantastic she did. She's in the form of her life, and when you see her run like that, you think you've got to have a go at the Mares' Chase. The National is definitely the plan, but there are four weeks between them this year. You've got a chance to do both, but she's good enough to run in a Mares' Chase - Bryan Drew, owner.

quotes.race: Coral Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Panic Attack is brilliant. She's a credit to herself to do that fourteen days later [after Paddy Power win]. When they're getting on you have to race them when they're in form and she's clearly in the form of her life. Harry [Skelton, jockey] said to run her and it's worked out. Tristan [Durrell] gave her a phenomenal ride, he's the most improved rider I've ever had anything to do with in a short space of time - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase (In Memory Of Edward O'Grady) (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: To some degree these wins are satisfying, but I'm a paid professional and like Roy Keane says, 'I'm just doing my job'. When Panic Attack missed the Plate in March we made this race her target. We've been second in this race a couple of times and I remember with Spiritofthegames I've never been more disappointed after a race. His owner Norman Lake was one of our first supporters and he died a couple of years ago. I love running horses. I don't shy away from it. I'll run them if they're right and sometimes I get it wrong. She won't come back for December and we will most likely go to Doncaster in December for a mares' race over the Christmas period. I'd like to bring her back here for the Mares' Chase.? - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Catesby Estates PLC Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race) (NHMOPS Bonus Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought it was going to be easier than that. I thought this was tailormade for Panic Attack, she didn't finish as strongly as we hoped at Uttoxeter so we put the blinkers on and she travelled sweetly. Tom gave her a great ride, she was brave and battled up the run-in. She'll probably end up a three-miler and she goes on the better ground. She'll go over a fence too - David Pipe, trainer.

quotes.race: MansionBet Cheers To 2021 Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were hoping Panic Attack might do something like that at Cheltenham last time, but she made a mistake at the first and was beaten after that. Nothing came to light, so we freshened her up and this was the ideal race for her - it's possible she's better on a flat track. It was a confidence booster for the trainer, owner and horse and we bought her to be a graded performer, which is hopefully what she'll end up being. She's always worked nicely at home and we've always had high hopes for her, so it's nice to get her back on track but there are no plans, although she'll get further. - David Pipe, trainer

quotes.race: Alan Swinbank Mares' Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Panic Attack knew her job and it was a good performance. She took me there with ease and it took me a while to pull her up, which is always a good sign. We were getting a lot of weight but hopefully she's got a bright future - Paul Townend, rider.

stable_tour.quote: She has an entry in the Ryanair just in case, but I think we'll go for the Mares' Chase. She's had a phenomenal season and I can hardly believe where we've ended up with her, with three wins on the bounce and a rating of 147. She's a credit to herself, flying around at home, and can't wait to get her out again. She'll get 3lb from the favourite, Dinoblue, so I think she'll go very close. 17-02-96

A very smart mare who was a winner at Cheltenham last April when taking the Listed mares' handicap hurdle. She added to that at Huntingdon in November when a 13-length winner over fences. Last time out we sent her to Cheltenham with hopes of a good show in the Timeform Novices' Handicap Chase, but she ran the oddest of races, as having made a bad mistake down the far side when going well I thought Scu would pull her up but she got it together again and ran on well to take fourth. She seems in grand order and the plan is to head to Warwick with her next for a three-mile handicap chase. I think she wants that trip now, and if she does then it opens up many more options for us. We will see how she does in that race before looking any further ahead. 22-02-23

runners.comment: Pulled up in recent Irish National but running well in January and could bounce back today
runners.spotlight: She'll find it hard to beat a peak-form Panic Attack and she was pulled up in the Irish National 16 days ago; however, she was running well in January, in a Grade 2 mares' chase at Fairyhouse (2m6f, yielding) and the Thyestes Handicap at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy; albeit no match for the first two); no surprise if she bounces back with a good performance today.

quotes.race: Mrs Paddy Power Mares' Chase (Registered As The Liberthine Mares' Chase) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything ran a great race again and I'm very happy. She does fall slightly short of those top mares, but she has loads of experience now. I thought she ran above herself and we will probably go to the Irish Grand National now - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Mahon Falls Mares Chase
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything is a clever and straightforward mare. She is genuine as you can get and jumps for fun - Sam Ewing, rider

quotes.race: O'Dwyer Steel Dundrum Novice Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything is very tough and very genuine. She won going away at the line. I was after my one early but she finds so much I was never really too worried to be honest - Sam Ewing, rider.

quotes.race: Ballygarry Estate Hotel & Spa Mares Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything did it well. She's a tough mare, enjoyed the ground, and she jumped very well - Sam Ewing, rider

quotes.race: Anglo Printers Remembering John H. Kierans Mares Hurdle
quotes.quote: They went a really good gallop, so I had to bide my time and Shecouldbeanything stayed on gamely. She's a solid mare and today showed she will definitely stay further. She's very versatile ground-wise, ran well at Cheltenham on soft and, while she has form on all different types of ground, that nicer surface brings out the best in her - Sam Ewing, jockey.

quotes.race: SP Or Better Guaranteed With Tote Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything did it very well. We went a good gallop the whole way and she was probably just in her comfort zone where she was. As soon as we straightened up and I got after her, she picked up fierce well. She's decent and hopefully can keep progressing. She handled that ground fine as well - Jack Kennedy, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Easyclean Tourist Attraction Mares Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything went a nice, even gallop and grinded it out really well. She found plenty and made my job a good bit easier - Donagh Meyler, rider

quotes.race: Howden Insurance Brokers Mares Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything is a good mare. She ran well in Cheltenham, probably did plenty and was keen enough so we said we'd have one run going to the last. She has a great attitude and she will definitely jump a fence. She won a point-to-point and winged from fence to fence so she will be grand.  We'll give her a break now - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Goggin Buckley Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Shecouldbeanything was very good. She was keen and didn't help herself. I held onto her for as long as I could and she quickened away smartly - Jordan Gainford, rider.

stable_tour.quote: She's been a smashing mare over the last few years. Imagine she has won ten times. That's some record. There aren't many horses who won so much. She wasn't herself in the Kerry National at Listowel. She'll be back and we'll try win a big handicap with her. 26-10-25

prev_owners.owner: Step By Step Supporting Independence Ltd

runners.comment: Progressive during this first chasing campaign but further improvement is needed
runners.spotlight: 9yo who has been progressive during this first chasing campaign, winning twice (2m/2m4f, soft/good to soft); she's open to further improvement but it's necessary now back up in grade, and she needs to prove her stamina; soundly beaten over hurdles on sole previous run in these cheekpieces.

quotes.race: CopyBet Supporting UK Horse Racing 'Chasing Excellence' Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ruby Island jumps lovely and slick and kept putting the pressure on the other one, and pinching half a length here and there. She has a bit of experience and ran well in a handicap at Cheltenham. All being well, her next race will be back to Cheltenham in April for a valuable handicap, which will be her Gold Cup - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet With On Course Bookmakers Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ruby Island seemed to get into a great rhythm and seems to enjoy it over two miles. Her first run over fences at Carlisle held her in good stead today - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qual) (For Ayrshire Yeomanry Cup)
quotes.quote: Ruby Island has run consistent and well for me and it was nice to get her head in front. She's run decent races every time and she grounded it out well, although it was very testing ground. I have half a feeling she might step up in trip again. I might bring her back up here again for a 3m mares' handicap - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Wilmot-Smith Memorial Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The mares' novice hurdle at Cheltenham could be a possibility for Ruby Island. She's very good and she'll stay further - Tim Walford, assistant trainer.

racecards.verdict: The Grand National was just 11 days ago but PANIC ATTACK departed very early at Aintree and will be tough to beat if at her best.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/5 Panic Attack, 9/2 Shecouldbeanything, 6/1 Apple Away, 16/1 Ruby Island

runners.comment: 31P in handicap chases, the pulled up probably best ignored; unexposed and needs respect
runners.spotlight: Blinkered first time when third of 14 on his handicap debut in this sphere at Thurles (2m5f, yielding) in January and off the mark over fences when landing fairly valuable event at Gowran (2m, heavy) last month; 22-1 and pulled up in Listed novice handicap last time but that had the makings of a warm event and he needs respecting.

quotes.race: Holden Plant Rentals Shamrock Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Jigoro has been running consistently and James [Smith] gave him a good ride. He found the best of the ground. Dropping back in trip suited and he won well - Ian Amond, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Mervyn Gray Construction Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was a good performance from Jigoro and we knew he had improved plenty from the first day. Obviously there was a lot of talk about Tom Cooper's horse and I thought it was a good performance. Jack was delighted with him and said he'll stay further. He said a faster gallop would have suited him but he was very happy with the run. He could go for the four-year-old hurdle at Limerick over Christmas - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: His form tailed off a bit in the spring, but he had put up some decent performances before that. He's going novice chasing and could be a dark horse . He's better than you've seen so far. 28-10-24

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late N W Lake

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late N W Lake

runners.comment: Mark and drop in trip ask a question but he's impossible to rule out
runners.spotlight: All chase wins around 2m4f, including win at this meeting last year; Newbury specialist who landed fourth win at that track when bagging valuable handicap for second time on penultimate start; never won off a mark this high and drop back down to 2m also asks a question but he's impossible to rule out.

quotes.race: BetVictor Greatwood Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham has fallen a couple of times, but he's only a couple of pounds higher than when he won this race two years ago. We knew that if his jumping came together, there was no reason why he couldn't be competitive. He's clearly got an affiliation with this place. He's got his jumping issues, but in a fast-run race on soft ground, he just gets into a better rhythm, and it's great he's been able to do that - Nick Pearce, trainer's representative.It's extraordinary when you look at the races Heltenham has been in this season, especially last time at Ascot. It's a good training performance, and he obviously likes it around here. He travelled so well, but we wanted to take our time and get into a rhythm, and get him jumping. I thought he'd definitely stay, and he had as good a chance as everyone - Charlie Todd, jockey.

quotes.race: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At BetVictor Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham won over hurdles at the start of the season and maybe had a hard race, but he definitely had a hard race at Aintree after that on bad ground. Before Kempton in February, his coat massively changed and I knew he hadn't been right. He's come into form and is pretty effective round here and we'll look at all sorts of races. Maybe Sandown and the Oaksey Chase will suit him at the end of the season, a big galloping track. If a Bravemansgame turns up in that, he isn't in his league, but there's a race at Perth for him and options at Ayr and he's in the Topham too - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Dransfields CIU Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham was back over hurdles and it was a bit different for him. His jumping has never been his forte, back over hurdles he was knocking them but he's gone and done the job and that's the main thing - Tristan Durrell, jockey.

quotes.race: Run For Your Money At BetVictor Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Heltenham is improving all the time and hopefully keeps improving. Chasing has helped him but time more than anything. I could see him one day coming here for a Coral Gold Cup, but that might be in 2024 rather than the autumn. More immediately, he could go to Sandown on the last day of the season for a novice handicap chase, but it would have to keep raining. He wants really slow ground, it's very important to him - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's done us proud over the years and hopefully there's another half-decent day in him. It all came together for him at the end of last season and he ran very well at Fontwell last time, although he's probably a little too high in the handicap at the moment. A big, strong-travelling horse, he wants to go left-handed on a galloping track on softer ground. He may go to Wetherby on November 15 and I hope there's another decent race in him. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Yard debut ignored; on last winning mark with first-time visor & Harry Cobden taking over
runners.spotlight: Three chase wins for Gavin Cromwell included comfortable win in good event at Ayr (2m, good to soft) one year ago; fluffed the start on stable debut in Cheltenham's Grand Annual but had yet to be asked for his effort when falling three out last month; now back down to that Ayr mark, while the first-time visor and booking of Harry Cobden are other points of interest.

quotes.race: Scotty Brand Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I bought him The Other Mozzie for Cheltenham, I wanted a few runners and I've always wanted to have a horse with Gavin so I took a chance and it's worked out.  He won well. I was standing with my brother Scott and I saw him coming on the bridle - I said 'please just jump the fences!' It was great, what a victory. I love the National Hunt and I'm just trying to get better quality horses coming through. He looks like he's one of them - Jimmy Fyffe, owner.

quotes.race: Race And Stay Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: The Other Mozzie was one I though the handicapper had been a bit hard on, but he was right and I was wrong! He got through the ground well. We'll go for another handicap - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: The Other Mozzie can be a bit keen so I was hoping they'd go a good gallop.  He's quickened well and won with a bit left up his sleeve - Kieren Buckley, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He was progressive last season, winning three times over fences and ran well in the novice handicap at Cheltenham. He could return in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham. He'd be stepping back up in trip and I'm not sure whether it will suit, but it might be worth a try. 04-11-25
He made a good start over fences when winning at Galway and has taken to chasing well despite unseating at the final fence last time. He jumps a fence well and hopefully can progress. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Veteran but 2-6 for this yard and 2m4f a plausible excuse last time; needs consideration
runners.spotlight: Veteran of the field but he won over 2m with plenty of give underfoot on first and fifth races for this yard, latterly at Uttoxeter in January on penultimate start; 2m4f a plausible excuse last time and he needs consideration.

quotes.race: Terrible Titties And Other Bitties Charity Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's nice to have a double and Sunnyvilla is a young 11-year-old, if you like, as he hasn't many miles on the clock. - Nicky Richards, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Betfred 'Bet Builder' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Judging on his Irish form Sunnyvilla likes to get on with things so we thought we'd keep it simple. He jumped and travelled well on that ground. He's in on Boxing Day and that'll be the boss's decision - Danny McMenamin, jockey.

quotes.race: Coolmore N.H. Sires Pyledriver Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Sunnyvilla can be very keen but he jumps for fun. This trip on heavy ground is ideal but he can go up in trip on better ground. He goes to the Doncaster sales in May - Brian Hassett, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Fairyhouse Members 2023 Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Sunnyvilla was more settled today and jumped really well. I thought the jump at the last sealed it - Sean O'Keeffe, rider

stable_tour.quote: He's a grand horse and ran a big race when a close second at Haydock just before Christmas. The ground probably wasn't soft enough and, if he'd jumped the last, he'd have just about won. He's a proper mid-winter, heavy-ground sort, so hopefully he can strike if we can get a bit of that somewhere. He'll be ready to run again in about three weeks and hopefully he'll go one better. 31-12-25

runners.comment: Rather lost his way; 185-day break may help but forecast soft ground also raises doubts
runners.spotlight: Won four of his first five completed starts over fences (2023/24) but just one success since, a Newton Abbot handicap, and he wasn't finishing his races off last year; 185-day break may have helped but this forecast soft ground raises further doubts.

quotes.race: Make Your Home A Happy Haus Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Blinkers have been the making of Fringill Dike. For some reason over hurdles he just lost his confidence a little bit, he didn't like being crowded. The instant we put blinkers on, he was just a different horse. Life is going to get tougher now as his mark is getting towards 130 and the better jumpers will be coming out before too long. There's a race at the first meeting at Wetherby that may suit as long as the ground hasn't gone too slow by then - Jedd O'Keefe, trainer.

runners.comment: Good second in fairly valuable series final (2m, good to soft) one month ago; progressive
runners.spotlight: Can be hit and miss in the jumping department but his profile over fences is generally progressive and he backed up February's Sedgefield romp with good second in fairly valuable series final at Carlisle (also 2m, good to soft) one month ago; respected.

quotes.race: Canine Premier Flex Plus Joint Supplement Handicap Chase (Go North One Man Series Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I thought the day I came off Coup De Coeur would have won or been second, so on that performance it didn't feel like he deserved to be the outsider of the field. - Brian Hughes, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: February's close second on penultimate start was a creditable effort; stable in fine form
runners.spotlight: Another ex-Gavin Cromwell inmate who secured narrow win over fences at Punchestown (2m, good to yielding) in June; 0-5 for this yard but February's close second of five at Musselburgh (2m, good to soft) on penultimate start was a creditable effort; stable in fine form.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Aeros Luck deserved that. He was very keen last day but he settled much better today. He's learning still. I would say he'll go on any ground but he is just a horse that can be hard on himself - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He finished second in three maiden hurdles before finally getting off the mark at Listowel in September. He received a high handicap mark after that, so he's gone on a break and we'll aim him at the spring. 10-11-23

racecards.verdict: It could be worth chancing Harry Cobden-ridden THE OTHER MOZZIE, whose stable debut at Cheltenham last month can be written off.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Heltenham, 7/2 Jigoro,  Coup De Coeur, 9/2 Sunnyvilla, 7/1 Aeros Luck, 8/1 The Other Mozzie, 16/1 Fringill Dike

runners.comment: Won four on trot in 2024; was then absent for 484 days and two heavy defeats since
runners.spotlight: Won four on the trot, all at around 2m4f, in 2024 (good/soft); was then absent for 484 days; needs to bounce back having suffered two heavy defeats this season.

quotes.race: Unibet Persian War Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Flying Fortune has taken a while to get the hang of things but is a good mare. She has a lovely attitude and has been very straightforward to train. Her mother [Turbo Linn] was very good and at one point was lined up for the Melbourne Cup. We'll go home and scour the programme book but I don't imagine we will run her again until Christmas. She's been busy and could do with six weeks off. We would have to look at the Mares' Novices' Hurdle in March - she's won that in a canter really - Peter Bowen, trainer.

quotes.race: Dragonbet Fixed Brush Hurdle Series Final Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Flying Fortune has been a star and looks like a different mare since we first got her. She's getting better and better. It's definitely our biggest win together. It'd be great if we could have more contests like this and she'll go to the Silver Trophy next at Chepstow. She's earned her place in a race like that - Michael Bowen, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Unibet Moneyback As Cash Races Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: This was the plan all along. We were a bit disappointed to be beaten last time, but the form of that has obviously been boosted in the first race, and I thought Flying Fortune's mark was great. She'll be going round the likes of Perth and Cartmel this summer - Mickey Bowen, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's disappointed twice now since she's been back from an injury, but I think it's ground related. If you go back through her form, she's not got anything on testing going - she got beaten in a maiden hurdle at Southwell on soft ground by a horse who was rated just over 100. She's not half the filly unless she's got quick ground and we're waiting for it to come. If it's right for her and she gets in, we may find something for her at Aintree and have a go. 26-03-26

quotes.race: Ferry Ales Brewery Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Pitwood Road had already won a 10,000GBP bonus at Ayr so this is great and it's why we've been campaigning her in Britain. The bonus is fantastic for British owners and British-bred horses, so it's opened our eyes a bit. Derrick [Mossop] has been a great owner of mine for the last few years and he sends the younger horses to us so we can go to Britain and race. He left her with us this season and it's paid off, so hopefully she can stay - Terence O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won nicely on her debut for us in a 2m3½f handicap hurdle at Carlisle in mid-December off a mark of 105. She jumped well and enjoyed the soft ground. I liked the way she battled on strongly to the line and it'll be interesting to see how far she goes up the handicap ladder. 31-12-25

runners.breeder: N J Henderson And Mrs S A Aston
runners.comment: Mares' novice winner last May; pulled up latest, but down in grade and one to consider
runners.spotlight: Uttoxeter mares' novice winner last May (2m4f, good); placed in two similar races late last year but pulled up on handicap debut in a hot race at Newbury last month; this easier; worth considering.

stable_tour.quote: Life has been tough for her. She was always getting little niggly problems and was a bit fragile, but we've worked through it. She was too old for bumpers earlier this year, so we sent her over hurdles at Uttoxeter in May and she won nicely. She'll be a novice this season and she can go well. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Dual winner over 3m here last autumn; not been in such good form since; cheekpieces tried
runners.spotlight: Won twice over 3m here last autumn (good/soft); hasn't been in such good form since but may fare better back here with cheekpieces now tried.

runners.comment: Ex-Irish; 2nd in maiden hurdle on stable debut; 2m4f on soft no problem; interesting one
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish; creditable second in a maiden hurdle at Haydock (1m7f, good) on stable debut earlier this month; should build on that; longer trip and softer ground no problem; interesting candidate.

runners.comment: Maiden hurdle winner here on soft; good run in mares' handicap over 2m4f last time; chance
runners.spotlight: Won a 2m maiden hurdle here on soft last October; mainly creditable efforts since, including when third in mares' handicap at Musselburgh last time (2m4f, good to soft; fourth has won since); chance.

runners.comment: Ayr winner in November; some fair form since; stiffer task now; visor replaces cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Ayr winner in November (2m3f, soft); some fair form in lower grade events than this since; visor replaces normal cheekpieces.

racecards.verdict: In an open race PITWOOD ROAD is taken to beat Just An Artist and Fresh As A Daisy with Atlantic City another to consider.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Pitwood Road, 100/30 Atlantic City, 4/1 Flying Fortune, 9/2 Fresh As A Daisy, 11/2 Just An Artist, 11/1 Spit Spot, 14/1 Tread Softly Now

racecards.race_name: Equine Products Best Turned Out Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners.comment: Cartmel winner on soft last year; two good runs over 3m in 2026; down in grade; chance
runners.spotlight: Winner off 3lb lower at Cartmel last summer (2m6f, soft); two good runs this year, latest when third in a stronger race at Wetherby (3m, good to soft); chance down in grade.

quotes.race: Vickers.Bet Independent Family Owned Bookmakers Handicap Hurdle (Cab On Target Qualifier) (Div I)
quotes.quote: The first-time blinkers certainly sharpened up Rioja Alta, who ran a good, honest race - Micky Hammond, trainer.

runners.comment: Four-time hurdle winner, including over 2m4f here; going suits, but stamina to prove
runners.spotlight: Has won four times over hurdles, including over 2m4f here last May (good); softer ground no problem but stamina to prove.

quotes.race: Coral "Daily Rewards Shaker" Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Follow Charlie is enjoying life a bit more, he's always been a bit tubby but a very good doer - Mike Smith, trainer.

quotes.race: Ayr Completes Juilia's Racecourse Journey Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I'm just absolutely over the moon, I can't explain the feeling. I'm not quite Frankie [Dettori] yet but I'll keep trying! I'd say Follow Charlie was runner-up last time to quite a well-treated winner, who then won again to boost the form, so it filled us with a little bit of confidence coming here. I thought stepping up in trip was always going to suit him. He's a real pleasure to ride, he travels and jumps fantastically - jockey Ben Smith, speaking on  Racing TV.

prev_owners.owner: Tor Side Racing And A McCormack

runners.comment: Hexham winner in 2024; fair third at Wetherby last time but soft ground not ideal
runners.spotlight: Only win was over 2m7f at Hexham in June 2024 (good); fair third at Wetherby last time (3m, good); chance on his best form but soft ground not ideal.

stable_tour.quote: He knocked his suspensory and went home for a holiday with his owners, but he's with us again now and is grand. There's no reason to think he won't make it back - he should be ready in the spring and should win at his level. He was a bit slow when jumping fences and, while we're not ruling that out, he'll probably stick to hurdles as he's more efficient over them. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Off the mark for the season at Musselburgh last time; chance off this 4lb higher mark
runners.spotlight: Consistent mare who got off the mark for the season in a valuable race at Musselburgh last time (3m, good to soft); chance off this 4lb higher mark.

quotes.race: Racing Post+ Ultimate Go North Brindisi Breeze Hurdle Series Final (A Handicap Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Bollin Matilda needed as many hurdles as possible because she jumps very well but she's very tough, she always has been. She was in front a long way but she wasn't stopping - Murray Dodd, jockey.

runners.comment: Best form on last two starts, both over 3m at Ayr (second of six latest); each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Two best runs have been over 3m at Ayr on last two starts, latest when second of six on soft ground; each-way chance.

runners.comment: 1-19; good third over 2m4f at Hexham latest; just as effective at 3m and soft ground suits
runners.spotlight: Has a strike-rate of 1-19, but was a solid third at Hexham last time (2m4f, good); just as effective over 3m and acts on soft ground.

prev_owners.owner: All Bar None Racing & Paul Drinkwater
All Bar None Racing & Paul Drinkwater

runners.comment: Second of four over 3m2f here last May but hasn't run quite as well since; new headgear.
runners.spotlight: Second of four on stable debut here last May (3m2f, good); hasn't run quite as well since but is now on a career-low mark; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

quotes.race: Free Horse Racing Tips At tipstersempire.co.uk Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: No Rematch is a heavy-ground horse and he was home with Mr and Mrs Rucker and didn't have anything wrong with him, but was just a young horse who needed time. He was always going to be a chaser and needs proper deep ground- Evan Williams, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: This horse won his only run over fences at Chepstow last season and I like him a lot. He's lucky to have the owners he's got because he's such an old-fashioned type, not a big horse per se but heavy-set, and it's fortunate he's been allowed time. I loved his run at Chepstow but it leaves us in no man's land as he needs two more runs over fences to get into the type of races he wants. He was born to jump fences when the mud is flying and will love very soft ground at a track like Chepstow. He's hard to read because he's a slow boy but I wouldn't have thought we've seen the best of him. 10-11-21

runners.comment: Both hurdles wins were in 2022 (3m/3m1f); 2nd in h'cap chase in March; not so good latest
runners.spotlight: Both hurdle wins came over 3m/3m1f on soft back in 2022; fair second in a 4m h'cap chase at Hexham last month (soft), but not so good last time.

runners.comment: Unexposed sort who hasn't shown a great deal, including on stable debut last time
runners.spotlight: Relatively unexposed, but mainly modest efforts, including on stable debut at Ayr last time (2m7f, good to soft); may do better.

runners.comment: Winning Irish point; ordinary hurdles form; improvement expected up in trip on h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Won Irish point in October 2023 (3m, soft/heavy; runner-up has won since); hasn't shown much in maiden/novice hurdles over 2m/2m4f but marked improvement expected now up in trip for handicap debut.

racecards.verdict: Irish point winner MILLFORD HILL can get off the mark over hurdles on his handicap debut, having shown little in maiden/novice company.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Bollin Matilda, 9/2 Rioja Alta, 11/2 Coylton King,  Pure Sirloin, 7/1 Jeteye, 9/1 Suspected, 11/1 Follow Charlie, 16/1 Don Brocco, 25/1 No Rematch,  Millford Hill, 33/1 Lennie Godber

racecards.race_name: Equine Products Best Turned Out Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners.comment: Ex-Irish; creditable fourth at Wincanton last time; conditions suit; has a chance
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish; bettered his first run for Olly Murphy when 3.5l fourth in a 3m handicap at Wincanton last time (good); has won on soft ground; chance.

runners.comment: Fair third over hurdles two runs ago, but fell when back chasing last time; bit to prove
runners.spotlight: Hasn't won since taking a handicap chase at Catterick in February 2024 (3m1f, soft); not totally disgraced when third in a 3m3f handicap hurdle at Sedgefield two runs ago (soft) but fell when back over fences last time; bit to prove.

runners.comment: Ayr winner in March 2025 and fair second at Catterick in February; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Won a 3m novice handicap hurdle at Ayr in March 2025 (soft; cheekpieces on for first time); best run since when second at Catterick in February (3m1f, good to soft) but well held in valuable race at Musselburgh last time; each-way chance.

runners.comment: C&D winner; good third over 2m5f at Kelso last time (form sound); goes on soft; chance
runners.spotlight: C&D winner off 3lb lower last June (good); clear of the remainder when 3.5l third in a decent race at Kelso last time (2m5f, good; winner went on to win 2m Scottish Champion Hurdle); has won on soft; interesting contender.

runners.comment: 2-30; two good runs this year, last time finishing second at Carlisle; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Strike-rate of 2-30; has a chance on her second at Carlisle last time (3m1f, good to soft) having also finished runner-up at Ayr in January (3m, heavy); each-way chance.

runners.comment: Mares' novice winner for Noel Williams; well held on stable debut but should improve
runners.spotlight: Won a Huntingdon mares' novice hurdle for Noel Williams in February 2024 (2m3f, good); well held on stable debut after a three-month break last time but should come on for the run.

runners.comment: Ayr winner last Month (second runs in 5.40); well held last time; wouldn't rule out
runners.spotlight: Beat Coylton King (runs in the 5.40) at Ayr (3m, soft) last month, but well held off this 5lb higher mark last time; wouldn't rule out.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

runners.comment: Worcester winner for Ben Pauling in 2025; pulled up both runs for this yard; bit to prove
runners.spotlight: Worcester winner for Ben Pauling last July (2m7f, good) but has been pulled up on both starts for Victor Thompson since, the first in a point, the second in a handicap hurdle at Newcastle; bit to prove.

quotes.race: Scottish Racing Academy Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Palm Beach felt like he was going half-speed the whole way round and he did that well. He's been working very well and I was hopeful of a big run - John Dixon, rider.

runners.comment: Irish point winner; not shown much hurdling, but interesting on h'cap debut after wind op
runners.spotlight: Won an Irish point in November (3m, yielding); creditable fourth in a Hereford bumper (2m, soft) on stable debut in January, but not as good in three runs over hurdles since; interesting up in trip on handicap debut on first run since wind surgery.

runners.comment: Chance on his Newcastle third in January but well behind Ck O'Mara next time
runners.spotlight: Fair third in a Newcastle handicap hurdle in January (2m7f, heavy) but well behind Ck O'Mara at Ayr next time (3m, soft); reverts to hurdles after failing to finish in two runs over fences (running creditably on first occasion).

runners.comment: Unexposed; fair sixth on h'cap debut last time; can pull hard so 3m not sure to suit
runners.spotlight: Unexposed maiden who needs to improve on her sixth in a mares' handicap at Kelso on her handicap debut last time (2m5f, good); can pull hard so step up to 3m may not be ideal and 2lb out of the handicap.

racecards.verdict: After his good third at Kelso, MAILLOT BLANC (nap) is taken to win for the second time this season. Roi Du Roume is next best.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Kells Priory, 9/2 Maillot Blanc,  Maura Jeanne, 7/1 Ck O'Mara, 15/2 Roi Du Roume, 9/1 Ebselysees, 10/1 Monsieur Le Fuzz, 12/1 Shighness, 20/1 Blue Indigo,  Am I Bovvered, 50/1 Palm Beach

racecards.race_name: Best Dressed Competitions Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Course winner who shaped last time as though this step back up in trip would suit; player.
runners.spotlight: 2m maiden hurdle (good) winner here in January; disappointed on heavy ground over C&D after but bounced back when a staying-on third on handicap debut at Ludlow (2m, good) last time, suggesting he'd be worth another try at this trip; respected back in a novice with Chad Bament claiming 7lb.

runners.comment: Has offered little in two hurdle runs since returning from a long absence.
runners.spotlight: Well held in his sole bumper, in December 2024, and he's offered little in two starts over hurdles (2m-2m2f), both on good to soft, since returning from a long absence.

runners.comment: Runner-up all three starts, but this step up in distance looks sure to suit; big shout.
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in an Irish 3m point behind a subsequent good hurdle winner; has since shaped with promise in a Wincanton bumper and maiden hurdle (1m7f; good) for this stable, the latter following wind surgery; not beaten far on any of those occasions and there could be a good bit of improvement forthcoming now going up in trip.

stable_tour.quote: His sire is starting to get some nice winners over jumps and this one was bought at the April sales after finishing runner-up in a 3m Irish maiden point-to-point. He'll start off in a bumper and then probably go novice hurdling. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Drops in trip but likely needs more time and experience before showing his best.
runners.spotlight: Showed some promise in a Chepstow bumper (soft) last month but he weakened markedly upped in trip on hurdle debut there (2m7f, good to soft) since, when running too freely; drop back in trip may suit but likely needs more time and experience before showing his best.

runners.comment: Has pulled up and finished tailed off on both hurdle runs, latest back from an absence.
runners.spotlight: Showed promise when runner-up in one of three bumpers in 2024 but he's only managed the two runs since, pulling up on hurdle debut last March and finishing tailed off when returning from an absence 18 days ago for new yard.

runners.comment: 1-11 in Irish points; faces a tough task on British/stable debut switching to hurdles.
runners.spotlight: 1-11 in Irish points but his recent efforts have been uninspiring back from an absence and he changed hands for £2,000 in March; faces a tough task on stable/rules debut.

runners.comment: French hurdle winner; wind op may spark improvement after a disappointing stable debut.
runners.spotlight: French hurdle winner (2m1f, very soft) in June, but he disappointed when sent off a short-priced favourite on stable debut at Kempton (2m, good) in November; off since but he's been given wind surgery and it would be no surprise should he leave that effort behind.

racecards.verdict: Parchment is feared following wind surgery and Crest Of Stars is respected but KILNEW SUPREME is narrowly preferred.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Parchment,  Kilnew Supreme, 3/1 Crest Of Stars, 20/1 Royal Rocket, 33/1 Winning Paddy, 50/1 Docteur Romeo, 66/1 Warfleet

racecards.race_name: Royal Ascot Lunch Saturday 20 June Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Cameron Johnstone-Baker rode over C&D (good) when winning easily with career best; up 8lb
runners.spotlight: 2-16 in handicaps, raised to 3m here (good) for last three outings; ridden by Cameron Johnstone-Baker last month on last two starts, runner-up before winning easily with a career best four weeks ago (Miss Tiara third); 8lb higher today but needs plenty of respect.

quotes.race: Experience The Thrill With Hottotrot Racing Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Lady Caro's a very clever girl. She's been so consistent this season, the step up to three miles has definitely brought about improvement and she's got a high cruising speed. - Emma Lavelle, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I don't think she wants the ground as soft as it was at Warwick on Tuesday and just weakened when you didn't want her to. She shaped like a horse with lots of ability and will come on a bundle for it. 02-11-22

runners.comment: Lack of impact in six handicaps, two over this sort of trip; different equipment this time
runners.spotlight: Down the weights but lack of impact in six handicaps (two over this sort of trip) prevents any confidence in her taking advantage; has worn tongue-tie and cheekpieces in recent starts, which are now replaced with blinkers.

stable_tour.quote: After a couple of disappointing runs early on she took advantage of an easier task when getting off the mark over hurdles at Chepstow in March. But she still ran green that day, putting in some awkward leaps on the way round. Her final run, when not disgraced in a better event at Cheltenham, suggests she's up to winning a mares' handicap and the valuable Richard Barber Memorial at Wincanton looks absolutely ideal. 04-11-25

runners.comment: 0-9 but she's a reliable sort and looks worth a crack at this sort of trip
runners.spotlight: Nine-race maiden but she's a reliable sort, runner-up at Hereford (2m4f, good) last time, and looks worth a crack at this sort of trip.

runners.comment: Staying-on 3rd to Lady Caro over C&D, albeit making it look very hard work in comparison
runners.spotlight: Had wind surgery (her second) before penultimate start; reportedly made a respiratory noise that day but performed much better when staying-on third of ten to Lady Caro over C&D (good) last time, albeit making it look very hard work in comparison with the winner; has 9lb swing in the weights for a near 7l beating.

runners.comment: On the premises on 2025 evidence but the 163 days off ask a question
runners.spotlight: Opened account at Newton Abbot (2m6f, good) last July and runner-up in three of her four starts since, at up to 3m3f; on the premises on that evidence but the 163 days off ask a question.

runners.comment: Won a 3m maiden point last May; beaten 56l, 46l and 63l in her three hurdle races
runners.spotlight: Won a 3m maiden point last May; beaten 56l, 46l and 63l this year in her three hurdle races (at up to an extended 2m5f) so does not have any form claims, and she reportedly bled from the nose last time; steps back up in trip for this handicap debut.

runners.comment: Just 3-1 when behind two of these on stable debut here last time; now tongue tied as well
runners.spotlight: 2lb lower than for Ffos Las win (3m, good) for Ryan Potter last May; soft ground might be blamed for two heavy defeats late last year and perhaps she needed the race when unable to justify market prominence on recent stable debut behind two of these over C&D last month; wore cheekpieces last time and also tongue tied today; interesting to see if her backers return.

runners.comment: Heavy defeats as hurdler; goes handicapping with a big rethink on trip but also 8lb wrong
runners.spotlight: Won a good-ground Irish point last May but heavy defeats in her four hurdle races; now goes handicapping with a big rethink on trip (last three races were at about 2m) but also from 8lb out of the handicap proper.

racecards.verdict: The safest option seems to be LADY CARO (nap) who has been a rising force since upped to 3m at this track and won easily last time.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Lady Caro, 4/1 Border Gem, 5/1 Miss Tiara,  Pooley's Promise, 6/1 Hurst Hill, 9/1 Jena d'Oudairies, 33/1 Poet's Muse, 40/1 Bee's Kiss

runners.comment: Not disgraced in tough handicaps of late; can be competitive in reapplied cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Hooded when solid third over C&D (good) at the end of last year and scored at Plumpton (about 2m4f, soft) on next start in February; revised mark has seen him held in two subsequent starts but that doesn't tell the whole story as they were seriously competitive series qualifiers; cheekpieces (worn once over hurdles when second here 13 months ago) are reapplied and he needs a firm second look.

runners.comment: 3m point winner who's up in trip for handicap debut; pedigree suggests it will suit too
runners.spotlight: 3m Irish point winner (favourite) who recorded similar RPRs in three maiden hurdles (about 2m, good to soft/good) across February and March; point win and pedigree suggest this step up in trip should suit; of obvious interest on this handicap debut.

runners.comment: Wheels have come off since handicapping; gets first-time visor from reduced mark
runners.spotlight: Won good-ground maiden and novice hurdles last spring but he hasn't fired in handicaps, including in a tongue-tie on his last two starts and with added cheekpieces (now swapped for a visor) at Plumpton a fortnight ago; handicapper is trying to help but others look safer.

runners.comment: Golden opportunity was missed last time; now makes handicap debut so 9yo may yet do better
runners.spotlight: 9yo who was 2-12 in points (the wins coming over 2m4f on good/good to firm); weakened on February's belated hurdling debut (soft) and couldn't convert what turned into a golden opportunity at Warwick (2m5f, good) four weeks ago; handicap debut and may yet do better in this sphere.

runners.breeder: V & F Berouards, Haras Des Sablonnets &
runners.comment: Won penultimate start; tired mistake exacerbated defeat latest; needs considering
runners.spotlight: 22-1 when she made a winning stable debut in Newton Abbot novice (2m1f) in September and was a respectable fourth of 13 in C&D handicap (also good to soft) in January; doubled her tally when scoring at Huntingdon (2m, good) last month but it was a tired mistake at the last when 15l second a fortnight later; still needs considering.

runners.comment: Heavy defeat on Friday; blinkers need to prompt a massive turnaround
runners.spotlight: Beaten just 2l when fourth at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good) earlier in the month but Friday's heavy defeat on similar ground at Exeter (extended 2m2f) takes some explaining; swaps cheekpieces for blinkers and her yard might have better prospects with Best Night.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Green Sky progressed well after a good debut and will likely step into a handicap or winners race now - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

runners.comment: Encouraging third when last seen in October; new trip can suit; respected on h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Finding her feet over hurdles and October's third at Hereford (2m, good) when last seen was quite encouraging; pedigree suggests this new trip can unlock more and she's one to be interested in on this handicap debut despite the absence.

runners.comment: Solid second on Friday and on the premises again if this doesn't come too soon
runners.spotlight: Landed a 'hands and heels' event over C&D in March and respectable efforts in two subsequent starts, latterly when second off this mark at Exeter (about 2m2f, also good; Green Sky tailed off) on Friday; on the premises again if this doesn't come too soon.

quotes.race: Betting.Bet Free Horse Racing Tips Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Joe (Tickle) said Taritino needs a bit of daylight and if he doesn't jump he can be tricky but he did jump. To be fair he was very free, I managed to get two breathers into him but when the other horse came alongside he lit me up again. It was a good effort considering. runners.spotlight: Improved plenty for first run and a break last year when stepped up to 7f in Galway maiden in October, beaten 5.5l into fourth; third has won since; off 177 days and type to progress as 3yo; up in trip.

runners.comment: Well beaten seventh at Bellewstown 11 days ago on debut; needs big improvement to figure
runners.spotlight: Well beaten seventh at Bellewstown 11 days ago on debut; wears hood; needs significant improvement to figure.

runners.spotlight: Gleneagles filly; dam 1m winner (RPR 77), half-sister to winners Square Dance (7f 2yo/1m), Concessions (7f 2yo) and Balcony (1m), out of smart 1m-1m4f winner; makes debut for good yard that doesn't have many 3yo runners on the Flat; market can guide.

runners.comment: Good form in three turf runs in 2025; below that AW 47 days ago; chance if bouncing back
runners.spotlight: Three promising runs last year on yielding to good, beaten 3.5l into fourth behind dual Group 1 winner Precise at Cork in September over 1m; below that when beaten 7.5l into eighth on AW 47 days ago; chance if coming on for that; stable in form.

runners.comment: Plenty of promise in three strong-looking maidens; handles soft; first-time cp; big chance

runners.comment: Bit below debut form when beaten 7l last of seven lto; drop in trip should suit
runners.spotlight: Stayed on well to finish fifth in Naas maiden on debut in March; bit below that up in trip at this track 13 days ago but only beaten 7l when last of seven; better effort incoming down in trip but likely not enough.

runners.spotlight: No Nay Never filly; half-sister to winners Dandhu (7f inc AW 2yo/turf Listed; RPR 107), Gustavus Vassa (1m2f; 102), Dutch Courage (6f/7f 2yo; 98) and Maid A Million (6f/7f inc AW 2yo; 97); dam unraced half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Rajeem; yard does well with 2yos and trainer won this last year; worth a market check.
