racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners.comment: Course winner; big improver last year; not in same form two starts this term; top weight
runners.spotlight: Four wins last year, including over a mile at this track on soft in April; won very competitive fillies handicap at Leopardstown in September off 5lb lower; not been in same form in two starts this term and needs a big step forward down in trip off top weight.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications Irish EBF Fillies Handicap
quotes.quote: We were delighted to see Pink Oxalis run well on the slow ground back in April. She is ground versatile. She wasn't right the last day in Leopardstown. The ground got very testing and where she was drawn, nothing was coming from her position. Jack gave her a lovely ride and she travelled very smoothly. I am delighted to see her back to form. The owners are here today, which is great. We will see what is coming in the programme. We were thinking about Galway. I think the small fields suit her and we will see how she is next week. We might look at another fillies' handicap back here and we will hunt for a bit of black type later in the season, she is capable of that. The horses have been running well. It has been a quiet month but we only have 20 horses in and we are focused on a bit of quality - Stephen Thorne, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Handicap
quotes.quote: Pink Oxalis was very impressive. I wasn't too sure beforehand on the ground but she won well over a mile the last day at Dundalk and she's been bouncing at home. She turned a corner and has gotten stronger. Her work had been very good although I wasn't expecting that, she enjoyed the soft ground - Jack Kearney, jockey.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Fitri Hay & Mrs Paul Shanahan

runners.comment: C&D maiden winner; improved for return to be beaten 0.5l lto; up 2lb but well-treated
runners.spotlight: Course and distance maiden winner on this card last year; improved plenty for seasonal return when beaten 0.5l into third in Curragh handicap 19 days ago, hitting the line much better; up 2lb but still well-treated back up in trip and enjoys soft ground.

runners.comment: Ran well off revised mark when beaten 6l at the Curragh lto; down in trip; each-way chance
runners.spotlight: Eight-time winner, five over this trip; landed 7f handicap at Naas on soft two starts ago; ran well off 4lb higher when beaten 6l into sixth at the Curragh 19 days ago; should go well back in trip and has won off higher in the past.

quotes.race: Colm White Bookmaker Handicap
quotes.quote: I knew Independent Expert would love the conditions. She had been running at Dundalk but she likes a cut in the ground. I wasn't sure if she was fully revved up for today. She's a filly that doesn't carry much weight and takes no work to get ready. You'll probably see the best of her fresh but at the same time I didn't know if she had enough done to be involved. Joey gave her a lovely ride, he took her back and let them at it, and then she stayed on well. A mile is probably better for her as well. The boys are excellent at claiming, they don't miss a beat and if there is any value, they'll take it. They were very sweet on her, they said she just needed a freshen up and she's obviously done well for the break. She has been placed in some big handicaps and ran in Royal Ascot last year. We'll make hay while the ground is soft - Denis Hogan, trainer

quotes.race: Nursery Of Champions Handicap
quotes.quote: The last day over seven, Independent Expert got a bit outpaced and stayed on well. Nowadays, the stiff mile suits her well. She was a good winner of a Killarney handicap last year on good to firm ground so we knew he'd handle it even though she handles juice in the ground as well. She's very tough, honest and genuine. The colours are important to me as they are my assistant Stephen Mooney's grandparents' silks. We'll opt for something similar, she might run well in one of those big fillies' handicaps on the big weekends as she has some good Curragh form and she'll be a nice filly for Galway as well - Stephen Thorne, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Indepenent Expert is a light little filly but the race conditions suited her. She was in well at the weights, so it's great she's a winner at two. It was a valuable race and the owner also has an incentive to buy another horse, getting a 10,000Euros voucher to buy a yearling at an Irish sale. That's it for this year, she ran well at Gowran on testing ground, so she could have a nice mark for turf handicaps early in the season - Andy Slattery, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She won well at Naas in a handicap on Royal Ascot trials day and hit the line hard, so the Kensington Palace looks a suitable race. She might not have as much up her sleeve as my other horse as the handicapper knows her quite well, but she's not been long with us and hopefully she can keep improving. The stiff mile should suit her. 13-06-25

runners.breeder: Hyde Park Stud & Glebe Farm Stables
runners.comment: C&D maiden winner, ran big race when third in Listed race nto; below form lto but excuses
runners.spotlight: Course and distance maiden winner on debut last year; ran big race when beaten under a length in Listed company at Fairyhouse afterwards; below that form when well-held in Group 3 206 days ago but that may have come too soon; stiff opening mark but open to improvement; one of three for yard that have won four out of the last five renewals.

runners.owner: Dooley Thoroughbreds & J Fairhurst & Deepak Dhand
runners.comment: Course winner; last of 16 on return and doesn't want testing ground; up against it
runners.spotlight: Won twice on turf last season, including at this track over a mile on good; last of 16 at the Curragh on return 19 days ago and doesn't want testing ground so up against it.

quotes.race: Membership At Gowran Park Fillies & Mares Claiming Race
quotes.quote: Gloriously Glam has dropped in grade a bit and she ran well in a claimer here before. She was sulking a wee bit on us and I'd say even the bit of juice in the ground has helped her. She ran a nice race for Jessie [Harrington] up the Curragh before the boys bought her online. She loves it around the bend there. She can jump out and dictate. Adam was very good on her, he took no messing and just sort of sent her. She likes that. She sulks a wee bit in behind. She will be able to hold her own in races like this and I think she will sneak a handicap somewhere along the line - Ado McGuinness, trainer.

quotes.race: Guinness Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Gloriously Glam got it easy in front which helps around here. She handled the ground well - Shane Foley, rider.

prev_owners.owner: Hambleton Racing Ltd XXXV & E Burke

runners.comment: Encouraging stable debut when second here over 1m 14 days ago; drop in trip will suit
runners.spotlight: Some useful form in Britain before being bought by current connections for 30,000gns; ran a very encouraging race on stable debut when beaten 4.25l by stablemate Sindria at this track on soft over a mile 14 days ago; nudged up 3lb; drop in trip should suit and one of three strong chances for in-form stable with great record in this race.

runners.comment: Improved for step up in trip when landing h'cap lto at Leopardstown; player off 6lb higher
runners.spotlight: Navan maiden winner over 5f on soft in October; returned this term in fine form, runner-up at the Curragh over 6f before going one better at Leopardstown over 7f (yielding) seven days ago; unexposed over this trip and definite player off 6lb higher.

runners.comment: Mark suffered after bolting up at Limerick seven starts ago; would prefer good ground
runners.spotlight: Bolted up by 8l at Limerick over 7f in June; handicapper hammered her with 18lb after and that has proven too burdensome since; did shape well [not beaten far behind Glory To Be in second) on return when beaten 4.25l at the Curragh 19 days ago but testing ground wouldn't be ideal back up in trip.

quotes.race: CBE Concannon Group Handicap
quotes.quote: That was very impressive and maybe the cut in the ground today helped, but also the extra furlong. Rion Rubette had been running over a shorter trip and she was unlucky to meet a good horse the last day. On her Curragh run, I thought she might get through and win but I thought she might only win by half a length or a length - Michael Butler, trainer.

runners.comment: Long losing streak but shaped well on return, third behind Glory To Be; on a good mark
runners.spotlight: On a 16-race losing streak but shaped well on a number of occasions, including on return 7 days ago when beaten 1.75l by Glory To Be at Leopardstown on yielding; has slipped to an attractive mark and a leading player if building on return.

quotes.race: Download The New Tote App Handicap
quotes.quote: Greek Flower won well again. She got a bit of confidence the last day and flew through that ground. She might take her chance again on Sunday - John Feane, trainer.

quotes.race: Navan Racing Festival Early Bird Tickets On Sale Now Maiden
quotes.quote: Greek Flower will be back next year. She got a great ride from Dylan, he rode her with loads of confidence - John Feane, trainer.

runners.comment: Galway maiden winner; found G3 company too hot after; unexposed; opening mark looks okay
runners.spotlight: Knew enough first time out to make a winning debut at Galway in September, beating Sanctijude by 0.5l over 7f on soft; never landed a blow in Group 3 company afterwards but very unexposed and opening mark doesn't look harsh; leading player for top course trainer.

racecards.verdict: An impressive maiden winner of course and distance last year, VARSHINI looks on a nice mark stepped back up to 7f

runners.owner: C F Harrington & James John Hughes
runners.comment: Curragh maiden winner; won conditions race 171 days ago; handles soft, hard ask at weights
runners.spotlight: Impressive Curragh maiden winner in August 2024; below that form early last season but finished well with a pair of third-placed finishes at the Curragh and Naas in competitive handicaps (soft and yielding) before winning conditions race on last start, beating Senna's Girl by a neck as 1-2 favourite; form of that questionable and he's not well treated at the weights here.

quotes.race: FBD Hotels And Resorts Castleknock Hotel Maiden
quotes.quote: Tina's Indian is a horse we love, we think he is very good. I've never had a horse to work like him. The owners gave him all the time he needed to develop into a horse. We were confident coming today. He is a huge horse and he has needed time - Mark Fahey, trainer.

runners.comment: Group 3 winner who struggled last season; ran well in Listed lto; drop in trip will suit
runners.spotlight: Group 3-winning two-year-old in 2024; struggled in three runs last year in stakes and handicap company; showed more and ran well for a long way from the front in Listed Heritage Stakes 7 days ago, eventually finishing eighth behind The Lion In Winter; should come on for that and step back in trip will suit; one of two for in-form yard.

quotes.race: Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (2yo) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: The step up to seven furlongs suited and Cowardofthecounty feels like a nice horse with a good future - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.race: Keadeen Hotel Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Cowardofthecounty looked like he could be a bit special at home but you're never really sure with a two-year-old until they go to the races. He's a particularly laidback horse and couldn't have been more impressive. He's big, well over 500 kilos, which for a two-year-old at this stage is a lot. He could go straight for the Coventry now. He's such a big horse I don't know if he needs to run again, we'll see - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A Group 3 winner at Deauville last year over seven furlongs, he's going to make his reappearance in the Committed Stakes at Navan on Saturday. We're hoping he's en route to the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot. We think six to seven furlongs is his trip and he's done very well over the winter and is training nicely. 24-04-25

runners.comment: Seven-time winner; ran to rating in Listed race seven days ago; shouldn't be far away
runners.spotlight: Won this in 2023; consistent stakes performer with seven wins; won Heritage Stakes last season, beating Mutasarref by a neck; best subsequent effort came when fourth in Minstrel Stakes in July; two starts this season, improved from return to be beaten 3.25l behind The Lion In Winter at Leopardstown seven days ago; down in trip; mightn't want the ground too testing but shouldn't be far away and trainer has good course record.

quotes.race: Bahrain Turf Club Desmond Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Lord Massusus disappointed last day but things didn't go right. We got him switched off today and he came home like a good horse. It was a good performance - Joe Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: The Dillon Marshall Property Consultants Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: We'll make an entry for the Jersey Stakes now, seven furlongs would be ideal - Joe Murphy, trainer of Lord Massusus

quotes.race: Irish EBF Auction Series Race (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Lord Massusus put up a very good performance and I think he's a good horse. That qualifies him for the final at Naas next month. He did what good horses do today - Joe Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Premier Nursery Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Lord Massusus was very straightforward and travelled well. He's plenty green, around here it's a tight enough track, but when I squeezed him he picked up and when he hit the front he pricked his ears and won with a little left. Hopefully he'll keep improving, he got the trip well. He's got a bit of scope and will make a nice three-year-old - Gary Carroll, jockey.

runners.comment: Promising third in Greenham last year; well beat on return at Curragh; could bounce back
runners.spotlight: Impressive maiden winner at the Curragh in 2024; promising third in Greenham Stakes last year but finished down the field in Jersey Stakes; disappointed when last of ten in Gladness on return 25 days ago; needs to come on plenty for that but still lightly-raced and handles soft ground.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Saracen was impressive. He had been showing up well at home and looks a smart horse for next season. He should come back for a Guineas trial of some sort in the spring - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: The straight seven furlongs at Ascot should suit him well and we were very happy with his run in the Greenham. 13-06-25

runners.comment: Listed winner in 2024; no impact in good company last year; down field on stable debut lto
runners.spotlight: Listed winner for Raphael Freire over 1m at Pontefract (soft) in 2024; never landed a blow in three starts last year, including in Derby; down the field on stable debut in Lincoln 38 days ago; needs plenty more.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Silver Tankard Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We all thought of Tuscan Hills as a nice horse and he's done everything right at home. We wanted to start him off over a mile like we did at Thirsk and we felt that, with the way he won, we'd move him up in company. We thought he'd enjoy the ground, although the track was a bit of a concern because of the undulations. However, he did it nicely in the end and he's a nice horse to look forward to in the future. We're going to have plenty to look forward to. He's showed us he gets the mile fine, but with the way he won suggests he'll stay a bit further and that's what you want to see from a two-year-old before their three-year-old season. Hopefully, he keeps going the right way and we can have a lot of fun with him - Raphael Freire, trainer.

runners.comment: Cork maiden winner, ran very good fifth in Irish 1,000 Guineas 332 days ago; big chance
runners.spotlight: Looked an exciting prospect when bolting up in Cork maiden in May, beating Bonus Time by 2.75l in good style; thrown into Irish 1,000 Guineas after and acquitted herself very well, beaten 4.5l by Lake Victoria into fifth, despite racing keenly; off 332 days; trip will suit; very unexposed and big chance, despite a less than ideal draw.

quotes.race: Annual Membership Available Maiden
quotes.quote: City Of Memphis has plenty of ability and everything she does, she does with ease. We were confident coming here that she would run a good race and I'm delighted she has won.  We'll take her home now, and aim to go up the grades, hoping to get black-type - Paddy Twomey, trainer speaking to RacingTV.

runners.owner: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
runners.comment: Highly-tried last year, couple of good efforts in Group races; ground likely too soft here
runners.spotlight: Sole win in 15 starts came in 7f AW maiden February of last year; highly-tried since; best effort came when beaten 2l into fourth by One Look in Park Express 12 months ago; well beat into eighth in same race 19 days ago; ground unlikely to suit and up against it.

racecards.verdict: It's hard to get away from the Paddy Twomey-trained CITY OF MEMPHIS here after two very promising runs last year

runners.spotlight: Out of her depth in maidens last year; mid-field at Leopardstown ten days ago on handicap debut; needs to find extra.

runners.spotlight: Ran three times at two, twice finished last; not a bad run on middle start; made a promising start for this stable when making most of the running over C&D two weeks ago; fair chance of reversing form with the more exposed winner Survivor's Code.

runners.owner: E D Delany & Mrs Lisa Delany

runners.spotlight: Down the field in turf/AW maidens last year; best handicap effort in November when not beaten far in sixth at Dundalk (6f); long-priced Bellewstown winner recently on first attempt at 1m, took the lead at today's distance; not guaranteed to uphold form with Imnotleavinyou.

runners.spotlight: Much improved when second at 50-1 in a 6f handicap at Dundalk three weeks ago on seasonal debut; encouraging that her best run at two was in a C&D nursery on heavy ground.

runners.comment: Took a step in the right direction with fourth over 5f on turf/handicap debut, solid form
runners.spotlight: A glimmer of promise on the second of three AW runs; took a step in the right direction with fourth at Naas over 5f on turf/handicap debut; form has been boosted by the winner Oh Cecilia and third-placed Bay Of Supremacy.

runners.comment: Leopardstown run last week may have come too soon after C&D fourth behind Survivor's Code
runners.spotlight: Leopardstown run last week may have come too soon after C&D fourth behind Survivor's Code; may struggle to reverse the form of that race with Monocle Rocket.

runners.comment: Got the better of a battle with Monocle Rocket here a fortnight ago, 5lb higher now
runners.spotlight: Two 7f nursery outings were respectable; appeared not to stay 1m2f on reappearance/stable debut at Navan; got the better of a battle with Monocle Rocket over C&D a fortnight ago; 5lb higher now, the runner-up may turn the tables.

runners.comment: Failed to run to expectations when 9-2 chance for recent C&D race won by Survivor's Code
runners.spotlight: Three unplaced runs at Dundalk; stayed on in mid-field over 6f on handicap/turf debut at Naas; failed to run to expectations when 9-2 chance for recent C&D race won by Survivor's Code.

runners.comment: Misfired gamble at Dundalk in February, huge price on handicap debut and ran accordingly
runners.spotlight: Misfired gamble in a maiden at Dundalk in February; huge price at Dundalk three weeks ago on handicap debut and ran accordingly.

runners.comment: Appeared to find 5f inadequate in his first handicap, can probably do better at this trip
runners.spotlight: Appeared to find 5f inadequate at Bellewstown in his first handicap; can probably do better at this trip; others have stronger credentials.

runners.comment: Runner-up when out of the handicap at Bellewstown, may reverse form with Dream Legend
runners.spotlight: Best run last season when third on nursery debut over 5f at Naas in September; failed to build on that on her last three outings of the campaign; much more like it when runner-up from 4lb out of the handicap at Bellewstown on seasonal debut; may reverse form with the winner Dream Legend,

runners.comment: Fair run on second AW start, never showed here a fortnight ago, chance is not obvious
runners.spotlight: Not beaten far in a 6f maiden on second Dundalk start; never showed over C&D a fortnight ago; chance is not obvious.

prev_owners.owner: Ms H McGuinness/Martin W White/Declan Sheridan/Breen White

runners.comment: Profited from a drop to this grade when third at Leopardstown last week, likely contender
runners.spotlight: Both wins came as a juvenile for Charlie Hills at 5f/7f on different ground types; has plunged in the ratings and profited from a drop to this grade when third at Leopardstown last week; likely contender with Reese Holohan's useful 7lb a help in easing his burden.

quotes.race: British EBF 40th Anniversary Novice Stakes (Sire And Dam Restricted Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The ground was a big unknown for Zabriskie Point. He was up another furlong in trip as well. It was testing out there and I'd say he put up with it rather than relished it. He's probably better on faster ground - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He won twice as a juvenile and wasn't disgraced when we stepped him up for a Group 3 at Newmarket. He's a bonny horse, but he has grown from two to three and enjoys his job, so hopefully we can have some fun with him. 17-04-24

After he'd shown a lot of speed at home, I felt he'd be a serious player on his debut at Leicester and he ended up winning nicely. His work since has been pleasing and he's got an entry for a valuable race at Doncaster in September already. 21-06-23

runners.comment: Has failed to make the frame in six starts since a Listowel festival fourth, hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Only three wins from 49 outings; placed seven times but has failed to make the frame in six starts since a Listowel festival fourth last September; hard to fancy.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought Secret Magician was caught for a bit of toe at one stage, and he got stuck into him. He's as tough as nails - Martin Hassett, trainer.

runners.comment: Worth a check to see how the market rates his chance relative to stablemate Hell Let Loose
runners.spotlight: E320,000 yearling and 3,000gns Godolphin cast-off; well-related; down the field on only start last season; had plenty of horses behind in a 1m Curragh maiden on reappearance; failed to improve at Navan; handicap debut now; worth a check to see how the market rates his chance relative to stablemate Hell Let Loose.

runners.comment: Career-best was in a C&D maiden two seasons ago, nothing of note last season or on return
runners.spotlight: Career-best was in a C&D maiden two seasons ago; nothing of note last season or on return at Dundalk 12 days ago; chekpieces for the first time now.

prev_owners.owner: R J Proudfoot & Mrs Ann-Marie Cullen

runners.comment: Showed signs of a return here on latest but held by Miss Americana and Hell Let Loose
runners.spotlight: Best known as a three-time Curragh winner; five wins in all, none since April 2024; weak form last season; well supported at Navan (6f) on seasonal/stable debut but was always behind and finished last; signs of a return to form  here on latest but held by Miss Americana and Hell Let Loose.

quotes.race: Mongey Communications Handicap
quotes.quote: Zephron has been great all year and has probably been unlucky not to win three. He loves those conditions and we'll see what he can do next year - Denis Cullen, trainer

quotes.race: Sentinel Ireland Handicap
quotes.quote: The cheekpieces worked out well over six furlongs and Annalise gave Zephron a great ride. She stuck to the rail and it's great for her to get her first winner at the Curragh - Denis Cullen, trainer.

runners.comment: Continues to drop in the ratings, well treated on old form, a top apprentice booked
runners.spotlight: No success since Cork (7f, heavy) in March 2024; continues to drop in the ratings, and is now 20lb lower than his winning mark; two runs this term not exactly persuasive; a top apprentice booked.

quotes.race: Buy Annual Membership Today Handicap
quotes.quote: Uncle Albert worked very well during the week. He is tough and genuine and loves that ground. There could be a nice pot to be won with him, although he is ground dependent - Kieran Cotter, trainer

runners.owner: Charles Kerwin & Brendan Kerwin & Liam Kehoe
runners.comment: Goes well for this rider, stable in fine form, ran a little below expectations last week
runners.spotlight: Breakthrough win came at the 17th attempt in a 1m Dundalk handicap in January under this rider; strong in the market earlier this month when beaten a short head into second on AW (1m); ran a little below market expectations at Leopardstown last week; Zabriskie Point has her measure on that running

runners.comment: Very closely matched with Miss Americana on running here 13 days ago, definite chance
runners.spotlight: Heavily raced since winning easily for this rider here last October; won again at Dundalk the following month; unplaced on his next six Dundalk starts before hinting at a return to form in two outings at the Curragh; very closely matched with Miss Americana on running here 13 days ago; definite chance.

quotes.race: King John's Castle Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: He's after winning three now and the only day he was beaten was over five (furlongs) at the Curragh. Between six and seven furlongs is ideal and today's ground was fine - Denis Hogan, trainer of Hell Left Loose

quotes.race: Navanracecourse.ie Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: He travelled really well. The shorter trip the last day didn't suit him and the bit extra trip today was more up his street. He likes him and hopefully there is another day or two in him - Joe Doyle, rider of Hell Left Loose

runners.owner: Patrick J Digan & Ms Yvonne Hennessy
runners.comment: Very weak form (turf/AW) since last July, sole turf win was in a 5f maiden in 2022
runners.spotlight: Very weak form (turf/AW) since last July; sole turf win was in a 5f maiden in 2022; not an obvious contender.

quotes.race: Dundalk Stadium Gift Vouchers Available Online Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Gobi Star was very impressive today. He's been a bit frustrating but it worked out lovely today, he quickened up nicely. He likes it at 7f but he can always go back to six, he travels well - Jack Kearney, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

runners.owner: Conor McKenna & Patrick J McKenna & Emmet McKenna
runners.comment: Six-time winner; out of form at Dundalk during the winter, in rear here 13 days ago
runners.spotlight: Six-time winner; out of form at Dundalk during the winter; in rear here 13 days ago in a race in which Miss Americana and Hell Let Loose were placed.

quotes.race: Bar One Racing Guaranteed Multiples All Shops Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: It took Rock Etoile a while this season to get back into the swing of things. Andy (Slattery) brought him back from a break and he ran well at Leopardstown a week ago and he was back down in grade here. He was drawn wide today but got out sharply  - Cian Horgan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Went close over 1m here on seasonal debut, Leopardstown run may have come too soon for her
runners.spotlight: Showed some ability at a modest level last season; went close over 1m here on seasonal debut with Hell Left Loose 1/2l away in third; Leopardstown run only three days later may have come too soon for her.

prev_owners.owner: Martin W Walsh/Lisgoold Racing Synd/Mrs Mary Louise Mulcahy

runners.comment: Six-time winner but his last success was in September 2022, no sign of the drought ending
runners.spotlight: Six-time winner but his last success was in September 2022; no sign of the drought ending; down the field in two sprint handicap this season.

quotes.race: William Hill Pick Your Winners Handicap
quotes.quote: Half Nutz is very straightforward but it just didn't fall right for him a few times. I was very happy with the way he ran in Listowel, he didn't get much of a run there. He's a horse that has to be ridden for luck, it didn't happen in Listowel but it happened today - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys GSB Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: We tried him over five and Wayne got off him the last day and said this was his trip. He's improving. Last year he was running a bit free and just a bit hard on himself but now he's as sweet as a nut. We could try him over seven now if something comes up as he's much easier to ride - trainer Sheila Lavery.

runners.comment: Has failed to reach the first four in 11 attempts, recent AW form is unconvincing
runners.spotlight: Has failed to reach the first four in 11 attempts, recent AW form is unconvincing.

runners.comment: Hard to make a strong case on recent AW form, more effective on turf, not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Three-time turf winner and often placed but 0-22 on AW and placed only three times; hard to make a strong case on recent AW form; however, he is so much more effective on turf that a good showing is not out of the question.

racecards.verdict: Rated in the 90s in Britain in his early days, ZABRISKIE POINT (nap) gave notice of a possible first Irish win with a recent third

runners.spotlight: Ran well in a Curragh maiden last June; handicap form has been largely disappointing; tailed off on final AW start last year; soundly beaten in sixth behind today's ribal Numidia before that.

runners.comment: Placed once, her new trainer appears to have a better chance with Bhean Saibhre
runners.spotlight: Placed once in seven starts for Willie McCreery; her new trainer appears to have a better chance with Bhean Saibhre; tongue-tie for the first time

runners.comment: Maiden has another run under her belt since finishing behind Bhean Saibhre at Navan
runners.spotlight: Maiden has another run under her belt since finishing behind Bhean Saibhre at Navan on seasonal debut; needs to improve from her Bellewstown fourth.

runners.owner: T & R Hennessy & A Fahy Partnership
runners.comment: In top form last October, needs to reverse the form of seasonal debut with Bhean Saibhre
runners.spotlight: Won four races last year, two over hurdles and two on the Flat, including her last start in this sphere at Galway in October; late-season form also included a Bellewstown second, splitting two of these rivals Idomything and Bhean Sainbhre; needs to reverse the form of seasonal debut at Navan with Bhean Saibhre

quotes.race: Callan Tansey Mares Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I wanted to get away quicker but You Make Me Smile got a little bit squeezed up jumping off but she got into a lovely rhythm on the second circuit. She was tough as old boots from the last and hit the line well. She has an entry for Galway on Monday so I'd presume she'll go there - Donagh Meyler, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.comment: More effective at Dundalk, fourth there on latest, 1-27 record on turf is a negative
runners.spotlight: More effective at Dundalk; not beaten far in fourth in a 2m handicap there on latest; 1-27 record on turf is a negative.

runners.comment: Not a bad effort here last time but has a bit to find with Prom Queen and Masego
runners.spotlight: Had one good run for the Gosdens, namely a Yarmouth second; moderate form at Dundalk; better here 13 days ago but has a bit to find with Prom Queen and Masego.

runners.comment: Much-improved when winning a maiden hurdle at Thurles, interesting with Colin Keane booked
runners.spotlight: Modest on the Flat last year; ordinary form over hurdles until a much-improved display when winning a maiden at Thurles at the end of last month; interesting with Colin Keane booked for his Flat start since joining Cian Collins.

runners.comment: Fair third when well fancied on seasonal debut, You Make Smile and Mystic Rose behind then
runners.spotlight: Generally dependable dual-purpose mare; stayed on well for a 4l third behind today's rivals Idomything and You Make Me Smile over extended 1m4f at Bellewstown (soft) last October; well fancied when third on seasonal debut at Navan; should be a bit sharper now and can uphold form with Mystic Rose and You Make Me Smile.

runners.comment: Four-time jumps winner, 0-19 on the Flat, fair placed form in staying handicap last season
runners.spotlight: Useful jumper, recorded a third win over hurdles at Thurles last October on her final start before a winter break; also won over fences at Wexford last August; 0-19 on the Flat but had fair form in staying handicaps last season; could pick up a race like this at some stage; trainer also runs Ethereal Star.

quotes.race: Ballagh Mares Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We had planned to give Bynx a break, and only for it being so near on nice ground that we decided to take our chance. Maybe racing on the Flat is buzzing her. Sean [Flanagan] said she was keen today but she has one thing and that's guts. She is tough out and when you have that you always have a chance. She goes up the gallop on her own and is a nut job at home. My young lad Jack is really training her as no one else wants the hardship of riding her. Jack is well able to ride but unfortunately is too tall to ride on the track - Martin Hassett, trainer.

quotes.race: Jimmy Shanahan Memorial Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: When in doubt, call Flanagan! He gave Bynx a masterclass of a ride and got the fractions spot on in that ground - Martin Hassett, trainer.

runners.breeder: Mrs James Wigan & London TB Services Ltd
runners.comment: Down the field in three races after beating You Make Me Smile at Bellewstown last October
runners.spotlight: Beat a subsequent hurdle/Flat winner You Make Me Smile at Bellewstown (1m4f, soft) last October to record her first win at the 11th attempt; down the field in three subsequent races before a break.

runners.comment: Never counted over a shorter trip here on seasonal debut, this distance should suit better
runners.spotlight: Best run last year came on final start when third over a trip just short of 1m4f at Killarney; never counted over a shorter trip here on seasonal debut; this distance should suit better; top jockey sticks with here.

runners.owner: Barrow Vale Syndicate/A D Mullins/Ms Margaret Mullins
runners.comment: Weak form last year, better when fifth here on seasonal debut, 3/4l behind Prom Queen
runners.spotlight: Showed some promise when fourth in a juvenile hurdle at Listowel last September; never far from the pace when fifth over an extended 1m1f here 13 days ago on return; ended up only 3/4l behind the pace-setting Prom Queen.

runners.comment: Can build on her recent seasonal debut at his venue, closely matched with Masego
runners.spotlight: Career-best when runner-up in a 1m2f Navan handicap last October, though beaten 5l; made a lot of the running before fading to fourth over a shorter trip here 13 days ago on seasonal debut; should strip fitter now and the longer distance may suit

runners.comment: First reserve, ex-German 1m4f winner, has made no impact in four starts for this stable
runners.spotlight: Won a 1m4f handicap on good ground 12 months ago in Germany; has made no impact in four starts for this stable; held by Mystic Rose on running at Bellewstown 11 days ago; first reserve.

runners.comment: Second reserve, 7f winner in Poland, weak turf form for this yard, a little better on AW
runners.spotlight: Winner over 7f in Poland in 2024; poor turf form in Ireland last year; showed improvement when switched to AW at Dundalk, putting in satisfactory efforts over 7f and an extended 1m2f before a poor run when well fancied last time; question mark about his stamina; second reserve,

runners.comment: Third reserve, placed in his last four races at Dundalk, effective on soft in France
runners.spotlight: The most recent of his four wins was at Dundalk in 2023; he has shown consistent AW form lately, placing in his last four races; effective on soft ground in France early in his career; third reserve.

racecards.verdict: A maiden hurdle win at Thurles suggests that ROYAL BELIEF has turned a corner. He may follow up wih Colin Keane aboard now
